'''Huw Price''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|h|j|uː|_|ˈ|p|r|aɪ|s}}; born 17 May 1953) is a British-born Australian philosopher,<ref>{{cite web|title=A Companion to Philosophy in Australia and New Zealand|url=http://books.publishing.monash.edu/apps/bookworm/view/A+Companion+to+Philosophy+in+Australia+and+New+Zealand/56/xhtml/chapter15b.html#chapter15sec33|access-date=8 December 2013|archive-date=20 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191020190739/http://books.publishing.monash.edu/apps/bookworm/view/A%2BCompanion%2Bto%2BPhilosophy%2Bin%2BAustralia%2Band%2BNew%2BZealand/56/xhtml/chapter15b.html#chapter15sec33|url-status=dead}}</ref> formerly the [[Bertrand Russell Professor]] in the [[Faculty of Philosophy, Cambridge]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Faculty of Philosophy – Teaching and Research Staff|date=November 2013 |url=http://www.phil.cam.ac.uk/people/teaching-research|access-date=31 December 2016}}</ref> and a Fellow of [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Trinity College – The Fellowship|url=http://www.trin.cam.ac.uk/index.php?pageid=321|access-date=28 December 2012}}</ref>

He was previously [[Challis Professor]] of Philosophy and Director of the Centre for Time at the [[University of Sydney]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sydney.edu.au/centre_for_time/people/|title=Centre for Time: People|access-date=28 December 2012}}</ref> and before that Professor of Logic and Metaphysics at the [[University of Edinburgh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://philosophy.ed.ac.uk/phil_history/index.php|title=History - The University of Edinburgh|date=8 November 2023 }}</ref> He is also one of three founders and the Academic Director of the [[Centre for the Study of Existential Risk]] at the University of Cambridge, and the Academic Director of the [[Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence]].

==Work==
Price is known for his work in [[philosophy of physics]] and for his brand of "[[neo-pragmatism]]"<ref>{{cite journal |last=MacFarlane |first=John |date=5 February 2014 |title=Review of Expressivism, Pragmatism and Representationalism |url=http://ndpr.nd.edu/news/46002-expressivism-pragmatism-and-representationalism/ |journal=Notre Dame Philosophical Reviews |via=}}</ref> and "[[anti-representationalism]]", according to which "all utterances must be looked at through the lens of their function in our interactions, not the metaphysics of their semantic relations."<ref>{{cite journal |last=deVries |first=Willem |author-link=Willem de Vries |date=8 September 2011 |title=Review of Naturalism without Mirrors |url=http://ndpr.nd.edu/news/25939-naturalism-without-mirrors/ |journal=Notre Dame Philosophical Reviews |via=}}</ref> This view has acknowledged affinities with the work of [[Robert Brandom]] and, earlier, [[Wilfrid Sellars]].

He was elected a Fellow of [[Australian Academy of the Humanities]] in 1994,<ref>{{cite web |title=Price, Huw, FBA FAHA |url=https://humanities.org.au/fellows/fellow-profile/?fellow_id=574 |access-date=2024-04-29 |website=Australian Academy of the Humanities}}</ref> and a Fellow of the [[British Academy]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.britac.ac.uk/fellowship/elections/index.cfm?member=19145 |title=British Academy &#124; Elections to the Fellowship - British Academy |access-date=2015-06-03 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151030032759/http://www.britac.ac.uk/fellowship/elections/index.cfm?member=19145 |archive-date=30 October 2015 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

===Machine intelligence===
Around 2012, Price co-founded the Centre for the Study of Existential Risk, stating that "It seems a reasonable prediction that some time in this or the next century intelligence will escape from the constraints of biology." Price voices concern that as computers become smarter than humans, humans could someday be destroyed by "machines that are not malicious, but machines whose interests don't include us", and seeks to push this concern forward in the "respectable scientific community".<ref>{{cite news|title=Risk of robot uprising wiping out human race to be studied|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-20501091|access-date=13 March 2016|work=[[BBC News]]|date=26 November 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://cacm.acm.org/news/157834-cambridge-to-study-technologys-risk-to-humans/fulltext|title=Cambridge to Study Technology's Risk to Humans - News - Communications of the ACM|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Around 2015, he assumed the directorship of the new Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence, stating "Machine intelligence will be one of the defining themes of our century, and the challenges of ensuring that we make good use of its opportunities are ones we all face together. At present, however, we have barely begun to consider its ramifications, good or bad."<ref name="phys.org">{{cite news|title=Cambridge University launches new centre to study AI and the future of intelligence|url=http://phys.org/news/2015-12-cambridge-university-centre-ai-future.html|access-date=13 March 2016|work=[[phys.org]]|date=3 December 2015}}</ref>

== Publications==
* ''Facts and the Function of Truth'' (Blackwell, 1988)
* ''[[Time's Arrow and Archimedes' Point|Time's Arrow and Archimedes' Point: New Directions for the Physics of Time]]'' (Oxford University Press, 1996)
* ''Naturalism without Mirrors'' (Oxford University Press, 2011)
* ''Causation, Physics, and the Constitution of Reality: Russell's Republic Revisited'' ed. with Richard Corry (Oxford University Press, 2007)
* ''Expressivism, Pragmatism and Representationalism'' (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
